description: Wisconsin Class M items from the September 2026 Motorcyclists' Handbook, including every printed Test Yourself item and the sample knowledge test.

questions.q: A plastic shatter-resistant faceshield:
options: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A faceshield protects your whole face from wind, debris, and a crash. A windshield is not a substitute.

questions.q: If you wait an hour for each drink before riding:
options: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Side effects from the drinking may still remain.
questions.explanation: Waiting an hour per drink does not erase the effects. Alcohol still hurts judgment, vision, and control.

questions.q: More than half of all crashes:
options: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph on open rural highways.
Happen at night.
Involve riders who have ridden their motorcycles less than six months.
questions.explanation: The handbook says more than half of all crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.q: When riding, you should:
options: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn by turning your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.q: Usually, a good way to handle tailgaters is to:
options: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
questions.explanation: Speeding up only makes the tailgater follow you faster. Change lanes and let them pass, or slow down and open space ahead.

questions.q: To reduce your reaction time, you should:
options: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
questions.explanation: In intersections, shopping areas, and school or construction zones, cover the clutch and both brakes so you can react sooner.

questions.q: Making eye contact with other drivers:
options: Is a good sign they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Doesn't mean that the driver will yield.
questions.explanation: Eye contact does not mean the other driver will yield. Be ready for them not to.

questions.q: Reflective clothing should:
options: Be worn at night.
Be worn during the day.
Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective gear helps drivers see you in daylight and after dark.

questions.q: The best way to stop quickly is to:
options: Use the front brake only.
Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes together. The front brake can provide 70 percent or more of the stopping power, but you still use the rear.

questions.q: When it starts to rain it is usually best to:
options: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane collects oil. The tire tracks left by cars are usually the grippiest path when rain starts.

questions.q: If your motorcycle starts to wobble:
options: Accelerate out of the wobble.
Use both of the brakes gradually until it stops.
Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate or brake. Grip the bars firmly without fighting the wobble, close the throttle gradually, and get your weight forward.

questions.q: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:
options: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
questions.explanation: Put beginners up front, just behind the leader. The printed key marks both A and B. The tail is the wrong place.

questions.q: It is MOST important to flash your brake light when:
options: Someone is following too closely.
You will be slowing suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.
questions.explanation: Flash the brake light before you slow more quickly than others expect, or where they may not expect it. A close follower is a reason to flash before you slow, but the sample-test key is sudden slowing.

questions.q: The FRONT brake supplies how much of the potential stopping power?
options: About one-quarter.
About one-half.
About three-quarters.
questions.explanation: The front brake is the powerful one. It can provide at least three-quarters of your total stopping power.

questions.q: To swerve correctly:
options: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly the other way.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip on the side you want to go. Press left to lean left. Separate braking from swerving.

questions.q: If a tire goes flat while riding, and you must stop, it is usually best to:
options: Relax on the handlegrips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the grips, ease off the throttle, and if you must brake, use the tire that is not flat. Then edge to the side of the road.

questions.q: A car on the left is waiting to enter the intersection. It is best to:
options: Make eye contact with the driver.
Reduce speed and be ready to react.
Maintain speed and position.
questions.explanation: The sample figure shows a car waiting on the cross street. Slow down and be ready. Eye contact does not guarantee the driver will yield.

questions.q: Who must wear an approved helmet in Wisconsin?
options: Every rider, at every age
Riders under 18 and permit holders
Only passengers
Only riders on a freeway or highway
questions.explanation: Helmets are required for operators and passengers under 18, and for anyone operating with a cycle instruction permit. The chin strap must be fastened. A helmet is recommended, not required, for other adults.

questions.q: Eye protection at night:
options: May be tinted
Must not be tinted, except photosensitive
Is optional if you have a windshield
Is required only under age 18
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required at all ages unless the windshield rises at least 15 inches above the handlebars. At night it may not be tinted or darkened. Wis. Stat. 347.485(2). Must not be tinted or darkened, except prescription photosensitive lenses.

questions.q: A cyclist under 21 may be arrested for riding with:
options: A BAC of 0.08 or more only
A BAC of 0.02 or more only
Any amount of alcohol in the body
Alcohol only if a passenger is also impaired
questions.explanation: Absolute sobriety, 'Not A Drop': under 21, any amount of alcohol is enough for an arrest.

questions.q: Two motorcyclists may ride side by side in one lane when:
options: Traffic is stopped
Both riders agree
The speed limit is 25 mph or less
A car is trying to pass
questions.explanation: You are entitled to a full lane. You may not ride in a part of a lane another vehicle occupies, except when two cyclists agree to ride side by side.

questions.q: Under ideal conditions, the recommended following distance is at least:
options: Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds
One second per 10 mph
questions.explanation: Count four seconds after the vehicle ahead passes a marker. If you arrive sooner, you are too close. Add space in rain, at night, or in heavy traffic.

questions.q: When vehicles are beside you on both sides, the handbook says the usual best path is:
options: The left third of the lane
The center of the lane
The right third, next to the curb
The shoulder
questions.explanation: A lane has three paths. If traffic is on both sides, the center path is usually the best space cushion. Stay off heavy oil at intersections.

questions.q: When parking at a curb, a motorcycle should be:
options: Parallel to the curb, like a car
At a 90-degree angle, rear wheel on curb
On the sidewalk
In the traffic lane with the stand down
questions.explanation: Park at a 90-degree angle to the curb with the rear wheel touching the curb. Up to three cycles may share a marked space.

questions.q: A cycle instruction permit is issued only if you are at least:
questions.explanation: You must be at least 16. Under 18 you also need a parent or guardian, driver education, and proof of enrollment in a basic rider course. The permit is valid for 6 months.

questions.q: During darkness, a rider on a cycle instruction permit must be accompanied by a person who is at least:
options: 18, with any license
21, riding as the passenger
25, licensed 2 years with Class M
18, riding within sight in a car
questions.explanation: The accompanying rider must be at least 25, have two years of licensed experience, and hold a Class M license. That person must be nearby, but does not have to be your passenger.

questions.q: In a staggered formation, the second rider should be:
options: Directly beside the leader
One second behind, on the other side of the lane
Two seconds behind, in the same track as the leader
On the shoulder
questions.explanation: The leader rides the left side of the lane. The next rider stays one second behind on the right side. Never ride directly alongside another rider.

questions.q: In a roundabout you should:
options: Enter without yielding if you are on a motorcycle
Yield to traffic already in the circle, coming from your left
Stop in the circle to let a truck pass
Use the left turn signal as you exit
questions.explanation: Slow down, yield to traffic on the left, give trucks room, signal right as you approach your exit, and yield to people walking or riding bikes.

questions.q: Where does the handbook say to avoid riding through oil and grease?
options: Anywhere in the lane, even when the road is dry.
Only the wide dry strip in the middle of a quiet road.
Big buildups at busy intersections and toll booths.
The left third of every lane.
questions.explanation: The usual center strip is about two feet wide and can be ridden when dry. Avoid heavy oil at busy intersections and toll booths. Wisconsin Motorcyclists' Handbook, lane positions.

questions.q: When you make a right turn on a motorcycle, you should position the bike so that:
options: A car can pass between you and the curb.
Traffic cannot fit between you and the curb.
You are in the left third of the lane.
You swing wide to the left before the turn.
questions.explanation: Move right so a driver cannot pass between you and the curb as you turn. Wisconsin Motorcyclists' Handbook, lane position when turning.

questions.q: Hazards are only on your right. You should ride in:
options: Path 3 only.
Path 1 or path 2.
The right lane line.
Path 3, next to the hazard.
questions.explanation: If the problem is only on your right, stay in path 1 or path 2. Use path 2 or 3 when the problem is only on your left. Wisconsin Motorcyclists' Handbook, lane positions.

questions.q: A riding group larger than four or five riders should:
options: Stay in one tight pack so cars cannot pass.
Split into two or more smaller groups.
Ride two side by side in one lane.
Let beginners ride at the back.
questions.explanation: A large group is easily split by lights and is hard for cars to pass. Divide it. Put beginners just behind the leader. Wisconsin Motorcyclists' Handbook, group riding.

questions.q: What does Wisconsin law say about riding a motorcycle between lanes of traffic?
options: Riding between lanes of traffic is not allowed
Lane splitting is legal
Only lane filtering is allowed, when traffic is stopped or slow
questions.explanation: Wisconsin: riding between lanes of traffic is not allowed.

questions.q: In Wisconsin, what is the youngest age for a motorcycle learner's permit?
options: 15½ years
16 years
15 years
17 years
questions.explanation: Wisconsin issues a motorcycle permit at 16 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Wisconsin motorcycle permit: 16 years at the earliest.
